Read before any task. ## Trust boundary (critical) GBrain distinguishes **trusted local CLI callers** (`OperationContext.remote = false`, set by `src/cli.ts`) from **untrusted agent-facing callers** (`remote = true`, set by `src/mcp/server.ts`). Security-sensitive operations like `file_upload` tighten filesystem confinement when `remote = true` and default to strict behavior when unset. If you are writing or reviewing an operation, consult `src/core/operations.ts` for the contract. ## Common tasks - **Configure:** [`docs/ENGINES.md`](./docs/ENGINES.md), [`docs/guides/live-sync.md`](./docs/guides/live-sync.md), [`docs/mcp/DEPLOY.md`](./docs/mcp/DEPLOY.md), [`docs/guides/remote-mcp.md`](./docs/guides/remote-mcp.md) (`gbrain mcp expose`). - **Run gbrain from cron, workspace scripts and hooks:** every caller goes through one wrapper that sets `GBRAIN_HOME` (never `HOME`), loads the brain's env file and runs the installed binary, never `bun run src/cli.ts` with an inherited environment. Log stderr (never `2>/dev/null`: a `no_brain` refusal then reads as "no results"), check the exit code, keep hook output off stdout, allow at least 10 s per call, and never print the process environment into a transcript. On a managed brain, schedule `gbrain sources refresh `, and have scripts commit the files they write with `gbrain git commit-push -- `, never plain `git commit` (`gbrain doctor --only cron_gbrain_home` flags cron lines that skip the wrapper). Wrapper and rules: [cron-schedule.md](docs/guides/cron-schedule.md#calling-gbrain-unattended), [scripts and the managed checkout](docs/guides/shared-checkout-git.md#scripts-and-the-managed-checkout). - **Keep a page to some members of a shared source:** put `readable_by: [alice-example, group:team-a]` in its frontmatter (a whole folder: `gbrain access rule add --prefix / --readers --source `, preview then `--yes`; widening waits for `gbrain access apply`) and bind each member's credential (`gbrain access member add`, `gbrain auth rescope --token *** --member `); `gbrain access check --token ***` and `--as ` preview what a member reads. A remote `not_found` may be a restricted page: check `whoami` before telling the user there are no notes ([Model C](docs/tutorials/company-brain.md#two-scoping-models-pick-the-one-that-matches-your-shape)). - **Delete or purge pages:** `gbrain delete --purge` skips the 72-hour soft delete, cascades to chunks, versions, links and facts, and `gbrain restore` cannot undo it. Purge only on the user's explicit go for that purge ("scrub the repo" is not one), one page at a time, verifying each; a stopped batch stays stopped until the user says again ([data-loss gate](skills/data-loss-gate/SKILL.md)). - **Bring in your chat history:** `gbrain transcripts ingest` imports a downloaded ChatGPT / Claude export (or agent session logs); `gbrain connectors` connects the account and syncs new conversations live, incrementally and on an opt-in schedule (cookie/OAuth credentials stay on your machine, 0600). Full guide: [`docs/guides/chat-connectors.md`](./docs/guides/chat-connectors.md). - **Debug:** a gbrain call failed, refused, or printed `[AGENT]` or `[gbrain notice …]`: follow the [agent operator protocol](#agent-operator-protocol) above (full contract: [`docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md`](./docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md)); `gbrain errors ` explains any code offline. Symptoms with who acts, consent and a verify step: [`docs/guides/troubleshooting.md`](./docs/guides/troubleshooting.md#symptom-table); database unreachable or `GBRAIN_DB_ACCESS`: `gbrain db-repair` ([`docs/ENGINES.md`](./docs/ENGINES.md#engine-detection-and-access-repair)); health checks: [`docs/GBRAIN_VERIFY.md`](./docs/GBRAIN_VERIFY.md). - **Sync held a file** (`Held : invalid_frontmatter …`, doctor `git_held_files`, `get_page.file_held`, `stale` search hits): the sync succeeded and only that file waits. Read it with `gbrain sources status `, preview the fix with `gbrain repair frontmatter --source ` (writes nothing), and ask the user before any `--apply`, especially `--include-ambiguous` interpretations; never retry a `put_page` refused on a held page. A source a broken file blocked before upgrading recovers on its next sync (`gbrain sync --source --no-pull` does it now). Write brain files through `put_page`/`capture` or a YAML serializer and check generated content with `gbrain frontmatter validate --stdin --path

`. Walkthrough: [held files](docs/guides/repair.md#held-files). A hold with code `invalid_fence` or `frontmatter_slug_conflict` is about the file's content, not its YAML, and the content-repair lane clears it by itself: the next maintenance run repairs what it can, `gbrain sync unblock --source --apply` does it now with a receipt per file, and `gbrain repair content --source ` previews every lane kind (its printed apply command runs with no extra consent). A hold the lane marks `needs_human` (a manual fence edit, a recommended page merge, an exposed tail on a world page) is listed in `gbrain sync status --source --json` with its paragraph: relay it, make or approve the edit it names, commit, `gbrain sync --source --no-pull`. Raising spend (`fences.repair.max_usd_per_day`, `fences.repair.llm true`) is the user's call ([the lane](docs/guides/repair.md#content-lane), [fence holds](docs/guides/write-refusals.md#invalid_fence)). A hold with code `preparation_stalled` (or a managed catch-up that stops `preparation_abandoned` / `preparation_systemic`, or a write receipt with that code) means the write owner stalled, not the file: no repair applies. Run `gbrain sources writer status --source --json` (read-only: the step, what it waited on, the owner and its version), fix that or upgrade the owner, then `gbrain sources retry-held ` and the sync it prints with the same options (`--no-embed` stays). Runbook: [catch-up stuck](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md#catch-up-stuck). - **Keep a managed catch-up moving without a human** (a live checkout where other agents commit while `gbrain sync` drains thousands of pages): a page that moves under the run is held (`concurrent_write`, `worktree_dirty`), a dropped connection is retried, and a relaunch starts a pass that admits only what is still unsettled. The operator loop is `gbrain sync status --source --json` (`state` and `reason`, the newest pass in `convergence`, `committed_last_10m`, each hold and the last error with `class` / `safe_actions` / `needs_human`), then, when nothing moved and `needs_human` is false, `gbrain sync unblock --source --apply` and the sync it prints; when `needs_human` is true, relay `next.user_message` with the slug. A plain status skips its heavy reads: a `*_read` field with `status: not_read` means that field was not read (never "none"); run its `fix` (`--detail`) when you need it. Decision table: [`docs/guides/sync-unblock-runbook.md`](./docs/guides/sync-unblock-runbook.md). - **Writes that ended without committing** (doctor `persistence_terminal_failures`, `terminal write failures` in `gbrain sync status`): the check separates active blockers (a recovery record or a sync checkpoint blocker: run its `fix.command`) from the unresolved pile and from historical rows that need nothing. Group the pile with `gbrain sources writer failures --group-by category` (read-only; each group has a fix and an exact drill-down), read one receipt's `diagnosis.fix` with `gbrain write-request --json`, and relay a group whose `needs_human` is true. Runbook: [terminal write failures](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md#terminal-write-failures). - **Migrate / upgrade:** `gbrain upgrade` (binary self-update + schema migrations + post-upgrade prompts), [`docs/UPGRADING_DOWNSTREAM_AGENTS.md`](./docs/UPGRADING_DOWNSTREAM_AGENTS.md), [`skills/migrations/`](./skills/migrations/), `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install` (manual migration orchestration without service installation). - **Eval retrieval changes:** capture is off by default. To benchmark a retrieval change against real captured queries, set `GBRAIN_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE=1`, then `gbrain eval export --since 7d > base.ndjson` and `gbrain eval replay --against base.ndjson`. For public benchmark coverage (LongMemEval, ground-truth scoring), `gbrain eval longmemeval ` runs against an isolated in-memory PGLite per question — your `~/.gbrain` is never opened. Full guide: [`docs/eval-bench.md`](./docs/eval-bench.md). - **Drive the brain to a target health score:** preview, then agree. `gbrain doctor --remediation-plan --json` previews job steps and the PROTECTED repair steps (each marked "requires user agreement", with its exact command and the `plan_hash` the approval binds); after the user agrees, `gbrain doctor --remediate --yes --include-repairs --expect --target-score 90 --max-usd 5` (`` from that `--remediation-plan --json` output; a changed plan refuses with `preview_changed`, so preview and ask again) runs the repairs (even when the score target is unreachable) and walks the dependency-ordered job plan, re-checking score between steps. The cap is cumulative across `--resume`; a paid step that would exceed it is not started while free steps still run. Without `--include-repairs`, repair steps are listed as skipped. `--json` classifies each finding `cleared`, `pending`, `consent_required`, `operator_required`, `explicit_kind_required` or `unsupported`. Stale extraction uses source-scoped database pages, including DB-only pages; it does not require a repository sync first. Empty brains (no entity pages) or unconfigured embedding keys hit a `max_reachable_score` ceiling: job steps stop with what's missing, while included repair steps still run. Three phase handlers (synthesize / patterns / consolidate) are PROTECTED — only trusted local callers can submit them; MCP cannot. Reference: [`docs/architecture/topologies.md`](./docs/architecture/topologies.md). - **Track a founder/company over time:** when an entity has typed metric claims in its `## Facts` fence (`metric: mrr`, `value: 50000`, `unit: USD`, `period: monthly` columns), run `gbrain eval trajectory ` for the chronological history with regressions auto-flagged, or `gbrain founder scorecard ` for a four-signal JSON rollup (claim_accuracy / consistency / growth_trajectory / red_flags). MCP op `find_trajectory` exposes the same data — read scope, visibility-filtered for remote callers. `gbrain think` uses this substrate automatically on temporal / knowledge_update intent (default ON; flip `think.trajectory_enabled=false` to opt out). Non-metric event rows (`meeting`, `job_change`, `location_change`) ride through the same pipeline via `facts.event_type`; pass `kind: 'event'` or `'all'` to `find_trajectory` to query them. - **Answer "who is waiting on me?":** connect the user's Google account once (`gbrain google setup` — two user interactions; relay the `[SHOW USER]` blocks verbatim), then `gbrain waiting --json` returns the ranked people waiting on the user, what they promised, evidence quotes, and Gmail deep links. Manage loops with `gbrain loops done|drop|mute`. It refuses on stale data and names the exact sync command to run first. Guides: [`docs/guides/google-connect.md`](./docs/guides/google-connect.md) (setup + every error and its fix), [`docs/guides/open-loops.md`](./docs/guides/open-loops.md) (how detection works); the harness protocol lives in [`skills/google-loops/SKILL.md`](./skills/google-loops/SKILL.md). - **Turn on System One decisions (TypeSafe Jev):** every slot is off by default and nothing is sent until the user opts in. With `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` set, `gbrain decide probe` (sends nothing from the brain), then `gbrain decide probe --query ""` to preview on the user's own brain, then `gbrain decide enable --recommended` after showing the user what leaves the machine. `gbrain decide disable --all` is the kill switch. [`./llms-full.txt`](./llms-full.txt) is the same map with core docs inlined for single-fetch ingestion. ## Before shipping Easiest path: `bun run ci:local` runs the full CI gate inside Docker (gitleaks, guards + typecheck, then 4-shard parallel unit + E2E against four pgvector containers plus a transaction-mode PgBouncer; unit phase keeps `DATABASE_URL` unset) and tears down. `bun run ci:local:diff` checks a doc-only diff in seconds (gitleaks plus the doc checks) and runs the full gate otherwise. Requires Docker (Docker Desktop / OrbStack / Colima) and `gitleaks` (`brew install gitleaks`). Fastest path, with a Ubicloud token (`UBICLOUD_API_KEY` or `UBICLOUD_API_TOKEN`): `bun run ci:ubicloud` runs the same gate across four ephemeral VMs in about five minutes, uncommitted edits included (`ci:ubicloud:diff` for the doc-only fast path). See "Ubicloud fan-out" in [`docs/TESTING.md`](./docs/TESTING.md). Set `UBI_OWNER` to your thread code. In a multi-lane wave, lanes run `ci:ubicloud:diff` or targeted suites; only the integrator runs the full gate. Manual path: `bun test` plus the E2E lifecycle described in `./CLAUDE.md` (spin up the test Postgres container, run `bun run test:e2e`, tear it down). Ship via the `/ship` skill, not by hand. Pass its test lanes the exact commands in [/ship lanes](docs/ci-event-parity.md#ship-lanes), so a passed full-ci run carries them. The full release + contributor process (CHANGELOG voice, version-locations sync, PR conventions, community-PR-wave) lives in [`./docs/RELEASING.md`](./docs/RELEASING.md); read it before shipping. **PRs carry no version** ([releases per batch](docs/RELEASING.md#releases-per-batch)): /ship writes a `changelog.d` fragment, and the release PR picks the next PATCH (never MINOR or MAJOR) and syncs every stamp. This changes numbering only: scope, merge, deployment, paid-work and validation approvals still apply. ## Privacy Never commit real names of people, companies, or funds into public artifacts. See the Privacy rule in `./CLAUDE.md`. GBrain pages reference real contacts; public docs must use generic placeholders (`alice-example`, `acme-example`, `fund-a`). ## Forks If you are a fork, regenerate `llms.txt` + `llms-full.txt` with your own URL base before publishing: `LLMS_REPO_BASE=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/your-org/your-fork/main bun run build:llms`. --- docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md --- # AGENT_OPERATOR v1: how an agent operates gbrain gbrain assumes an AI agent is its operator. Every failure, refusal, degraded result and recommendation gbrain produces (MCP tool results, CLI human output, CLI `--json`, doctor, readiness) carries the same machine contract: a stable `code`, a reason, one next step with who acts and whether the user must agree first, and a read-only way to verify it worked. This page is that contract, `contract_version: 1`. Related pages: [error codes](../guides/error-codes.md) (one row per `code`; offline: `gbrain errors `), [exit codes](../guides/exit-codes.md), [`_meta` channels](MCP_META_CHANNELS.md), [memory verbs](MEMORY_VERBS_v1.md). ## Quick contract 1. Read `code` (fall back to `error` on older servers). `message` says what happened, `why` says why. 2. Follow `fix.next`: - `run` → run `fix.argv` (CLI) or call `fix.mcp` (MCP) exactly as given. - `ask_user` → relay `user_message` to the user and stop; run the fix only after they agree. - `tell_user_to_run` → give the user `fix.command`; it needs them or the brain host's operator. - `wait` → retry after the stated delay with the same request. - `report` → tell the user what happened and run `gbrain doctor --json`. 3. Then run `fix.verify` (always read-only) to confirm the fix worked. 4. Treat `[gbrain notice …]` blocks and `[AGENT]` blocks the same way. A degraded result is not proof of "no notes": a result stamped `[gbrain degraded: …]` (`_meta.degraded`, the CLI `degraded` key) is partial. ## Transcripts These are generated from the frozen wire goldens in `test/fixtures/agent-contract/v1/` by `bun run build:agent-protocol`; the goldens never store `next`, so the generator recomputes it with the same decision table gbrain uses at render time. Docs URLs on the wire are pinned to the installed version; the transcripts show `master`. Transcripts marked "journey" are recorded from real CLI and stdio MCP runs by the deterministic agent journey (`test/agent-journey.serial.test.ts`); machine values (home directory, pids, ids, times) show as fixed examples. ### 1. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off.", "options": [ { "id": "on", "label": "Keep the conversation archive on (in effect now)" }, { "id": "off", "label": "Turn the conversation archive off", "argv": [ "gbrain", "transcripts", "archive", "off" ] } ], "default": "on", "default_reason": "In effect now: on by default on a personal brain; nothing needs an answer." } ], "contract_version": 1 } ], "contract_version": 1 } ``` stdout is one document; the brain is ready and nothing blocks using it. The agent first does the `harness_wiring` step: connecting gbrain to itself is part of the install, not a setting. It then reports the install and relays the `first_run_decisions` `user_message` ("gbrain is installed. In effect: search mode conservative; agents save only what you ask them to remember, until you turn on automatic saving (salient is recommended: durable facts you state, saved with provenance). Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $160, balanced $10 / $200 / $400, tokenmax $20 / $400 / $800 per month. Nothing needs an answer now; tell me any time if you want to change any of these, and I'll apply it.") once in that reply, without waiting for an answer. The settings in effect are `search_mode` (default `conservative`), `writeback` (default `off`), `upkeep` (default `on`), `conversation_archive` (default `on`); each option carries the exact argv to apply it when the user picks one. ### 5. A caller mistake over stdio MCP, recorded: `run` (journey) A harness on `gbrain serve --surface verbs` passes a string where `recall` expects a number (H1a journey, recorded from a real stdio session). ```text recall {"query":"quokka-journey-marker","limit":"abc"} ``` gbrain returns (`isError: true`, the envelope shown parsed): ```json { "error": "invalid_params", "code": "invalid_params", "message": "Parameter \"limit\" must be a number", "suggestion": "Pass `limit` as a number (Per-arm max (default 50, cap 100)). Example: recall {\"limit\": 10}. Next: recall {\"query\":\"quokka-journey-marker\",\"limit\":10}", "docs": "https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/error-codes.md#invalid_params", "protocol_version": 1, "fix": { "mcp": { "tool": "recall", "arguments": { "query": "quokka-journey-marker", "limit": 10 } }, "consent": [], "actor": "agent", "next": "run", "why": "The call failed validation before it ran, so nothing changed. This is the same call with your other arguments kept and `limit` set to 10.", "requires_exclusive": false }, "docs_cmd": [ "gbrain", "errors", "invalid_params" ], "class": "caller", "retryable": false, "contract_version": 1 } ``` One content block, `code: invalid_params`, `class: caller`. Nothing ran, so `fix.next: run`: the agent calls `recall {"query":"quokka-journey-marker","limit":10}` exactly as given (its other arguments kept, the bad one corrected) and gets the recall it wanted. ### 6. A second session on a locked brain: status-only serve, `tell_user_to_run` (journey) A second agent session starts `gbrain serve` while another session's serve owns the PGLite brain. The handshake still completes, with one tool, `gbrain_status` (H1a journey, recorded). ```text gbrain_status {} ``` gbrain returns these content blocks: `content[0]`: ```json { "status": "unavailable", "reason": "lock_held", "why": "This brain (/home/alice-example/.gbrain/brain.pglite) is open in another `gbrain serve` (PID 48213), usually started by another agent session, so this server cannot open it.", "brain_path": "/home/alice-example/.gbrain/brain.pglite", "config_path": "/home/alice-example/.gbrain/config.json", "lock_owner": { "pid": "48213", "transport": "stdio", "serve": true }, "fix": { "mcp": { "tool": "gbrain_status", "arguments": {} }, "consent": [], "actor": "user", "next": "tell_user_to_run", "why": "Close the session that owns the brain (another `gbrain serve` (PID 48213), usually started by another agent session); then call gbrain_status again and this server opens the brain in place (re-checked at most every 5 s). If your client does not refresh its tool list after recovery, restart this MCP server.", "user_message": "Your gbrain brain is already open in another gbrain serve (PID 48213), usually started by another agent session, so this session can't use memory right now. Close that session and I'll reconnect, or I can set up one shared gbrain server so both sessions work at once. Which do you prefer?", "requires_exclusive": false }, "user_message": "Your gbrain brain is already open in another gbrain serve (PID 48213), usually started by another agent session, so this session can't use memory right now. Close that session and I'll reconnect, or I can set up one shared gbrain server so both sessions work at once. Which do you prefer?", "decisions": [ { "id": "lock_recovery", "question": "Two agent sessions want the same brain. Close the other session, or share one HTTP server?", "options": [ { "id": "close_owner", "label": "Close another gbrain serve (PID 48213), usually started by another agent session; this server recovers on the next gbrain_status call." }, { "id": "share_http", "label": "Run one shared `gbrain serve --http` and connect every harness to it (writes harness config, mints tokens); the full plan is share_http_plan.", "argv": [ "kill", "48213" ] } ], "default": "close_owner", "default_reason": "Nothing is installed or reconfigured; the brain comes back as soon as the other session ends." } ], "share_http_plan": { "argv": [ "kill", "48213" ], "command": "kill 48213", "consent": [], "actor": "user", "why": "Stop another `gbrain serve` (PID 48213), usually started by another agent session first (or quit that session); the shared server needs the brain's single-writer lock.", "requires_exclusive": false, "then": { "argv": [ "gbrain", "serve", "--http" ], "command": "gbrain serve --http", "consent": [ "persistent_install" ], "actor": "user", "why": "Run ONE shared HTTP server for every agent session on this machine (keep it running, e.g. under autopilot or a terminal).", "requires_exclusive": true, "then": { "argv": [ "gbrain", "bootstrap", "harness", "--harness", "all", "--yes" ], "command": "gbrain bootstrap harness --harness all --yes", "consent": [ "persistent_install", "credentials" ], "actor": "user", "why": "Mints one bearer token per detected harness through the running HTTP server and rewrites each harness MCP entry to it (each stdio entry keeps working until its harness is rewired).", "user_message": "I can connect your agent apps to the shared gbrain server so every session uses memory at once. That stores an access token in each app's config and pre-approves gbrain's tools. OK?", "verify": { "argv": [ "gbrain", "doctor", "--only", "harness_wiring", "--json" ] }, "docs": "https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/remote-mcp.md", "requires_exclusive": false } } }, "checked_at": "2026-10-03T16:20:00.000Z", "contract_version": 1, "surface": "full", "surface_source": "default" } ``` `reason: lock_held` names the owner (`lock_owner.pid`). `fix.next` is `tell_user_to_run` because only the user can close the other session: the agent relays `user_message` and offers `close_owner` or `share_http`. Calling `gbrain_status` again after the owner exits opens the brain in place and the full tool list arrives through `tools/list_changed`. ## The error envelope One shape for every error: the CLI `--json` document, the single content block of an MCP `isError` result, and HTTP error bodies. | Field | Type | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `error` | string | Legacy wire value, frozen forever under v1. Equals `code` except for the four legacy values listed under **Precedence** below. | | `code` | string | Canonical registry code ([error codes](../guides/error-codes.md)). | | `reason` | string? | Sub-cause where one code covers several (`embeddings_disabled`, `wired_running`, …). | | `message` | string | What happened, one sentence. | | `suggestion` | string | Prose next step. When `fix` exists its rendered command is appended, so the two never disagree. | | `why` | string? | Enough context to explain the failure and weigh tradeoffs. | | `fix` | RenderedAction? | The next step (below). | | `docs` | string? | Absolute URL, pinned to the installed version (`master` for source checkouts, `LLMS_REPO_BASE` for forks). | | `docs_cmd` | string[] | `["gbrain","errors",""]`: the same row, offline. | | `class` | enum | `caller` · `consent` · `retryable` · `unavailable` · `server` · `host_only`. | | `retryable` | boolean | True only when a retry with the same request identity is safe. | | `notices` | RenderedNotice[]? | Notices attached to an error result (see below). | | `contract_version` | `1` | This contract. | Pre-existing keys keep their names and meaning: `detail`, `protocol_version` (memory verbs), `write_request` and `write_error` (write receipts). **Precedence.** Read `code`; fall back to `error` when `code` is absent (a server older than v1). Four surfaces send a legacy `error` value that differs from `code`; the canonical value rides `code`: | `error` (frozen) | `code` (canonical) | |---|---| | `unknown_operation` (HTTP unknown op) | `unknown_tool` | | `invalid_params` (jobs not found) | `not_found` | | `page_identity_changed` (page missing during write replay) | `page_not_found` | | the scope failure's existing value (`permission_denied`, `missing_scope`) | `insufficient_scope` | `gbrain errors --changed` lists these offline. Memory verbs keep their frozen v1 codes and `protocol_version: 1`, and gain `code` with the same value. **Safe recovery.** A mutating call whose outcome is unknown never says "retry". Its `fix` points at the evidence: your own write receipt (`get_write_request {request_id}` over MCP, `gbrain write-request -- ` on the CLI), the op's own status read (`submit_job` → `get_job`), or a host inspection by the brain's operator when the receipt belongs to someone else. `retryable: true` appears only on idempotent ops when the retry reuses the same request identity. **Unknown failures** come back as `code: "internal_error"` naming the op, with `next: report`: tell the user, run `gbrain doctor --json` on the brain host, and report it if it repeats. ## The fix: `Action` ```ts interface RenderedAction { argv?: string[]; // ['gbrain', …]: explicit --brain/--source; positionals after '--' command?: string; // shell-quoted from argv; never hand-built mcp?: { tool: string; arguments: Record }; // present when callable on your connection (or relayed: see below) consent: Effect[]; // [] means no consent needed actor: 'agent' | 'user' | 'host_admin' | 'provider'; next: 'run' | 'ask_user' | 'tell_user_to_run' | 'wait' | 'report'; why: string; user_message?: string; // relay text for the user, verbatim verify?: { argv?: string[]; mcp?: McpCall }; // read-only docs?: string; // absolute URL requires_exclusive: boolean; // needs the brain's single-writer lock inputs?: { name: string; how: string }[]; // values you must obtain first; argv holds `` only for these plan_hash?: string; // destructive/maintenance: binds the approved selection preview_argv?: string[]; // read-only preview of the same plan then?: RenderedAction; // step two of a two-step plan } ``` **Explicit routing.** Every `gbrain` argv in a fix (`argv`, `preview_argv`, `verify.argv`, `then`) names the brain and source the failing call acted on: `--brain ` for commands that open a brain, `--source ` for commands that resolve their source through the ambient chain (shared ops, and CLI commands the command table marks `routes_source`; `gbrain extract`, whose `--source` is the fs|db mode, gets `--source-id `). gbrain appends them when it renders the fix, before any bare `--`, and keeps flags the fix already carries. So you can run the fix later from another directory, or under a different `GBRAIN_BRAIN_ID`, `GBRAIN_SOURCE`, `.gbrain-mount` or `.gbrain-source`, and it still acts on the intended brain. Over HTTP only the source id is pinned, and only where a thin client can send it (an op with a `source_id` scope, or a command the brain host's operator runs): a mount id is host topology, and a thin client refuses `--brain`. Paths are stripped as everywhere else. A thin client pins nothing of its own: it has no local mounts and its remote scopes the source. `next` is computed when gbrain renders the fix for your connection: from the effects, the actor, the transport, which tools you can call and the user's preapprovals. It is never stored, so the same fix can say `run` on the CLI and `tell_user_to_run` over MCP. When a fix has `inputs` (for example a model's per-token price), obtain each value as `how` describes and substitute it for `` before running. ### Effects | Effect | Means | What authorizes it | |---|---|---| | `paid` | spends money with a provider | `--yes` (cap derived from the estimate × 1.5, floor $0.25), `--max-usd`/`--max-cost`, `spend.posture=tokenmax`, or the user's per-run preapproval | | `destructive` | deletes or rewrites data | `--yes --expect ` only; never preapprovable | | `credentials` | creates, stores or sends a credential | `--yes` (or the command's `--apply`/`--trust`) | | `egress` | sends brain content off the machine | `--yes` (or `--apply`/`--trust`) | | `persistent_install` | installs a service, hook, registration or scheduled job | `--yes`, the command's `--apply`, or the user's install preapproval (never covers credentials) | ### Actors | Actor | Who runs the fix | |---|---| | `agent` | you | | `user` | the user, in their own terminal or app (for example a credential prompt, or a CLI-only fix while you are on stdio MCP) | | `host_admin` | the operator of the brain host (a remote brain over HTTP, scope grants, server restarts). Never authorizable from MCP | | `provider` | an outside service you wait on (rate limits, outages) | A fix expected to run past 120 s (`AGENT_TOOL_LIMIT_MS`) is never `agent`; it renders `tell_user_to_run`. ### The `next` decision table First matching row wins. | # | Condition | `next` | |---|---|---| | 1 | the stored fix asks the user (a refusal whose every way out is the user's decision, such as `owner_unavailable` with `detail: unbound_source`) | `ask_user` | | 2 | no runnable step (no `argv`, no callable `mcp`, and not an MCP-only fix on the CLI) | `report`: relay `message`; run `gbrain doctor --json` where you can | | 3 | `actor = provider` | `wait`: retry after the stated delay with the same request identity | | 4 | `actor` is `user` or `host_admin`, or the fix is CLI-only and you are on MCP, or MCP-only and you are on the CLI | `tell_user_to_run` | | 5 | `consent` is non-empty and not covered by a matching preapproval (`destructive` never is) | `ask_user` | | 6 | otherwise | `run` | A CLI-only fix rendered for an MCP caller gets actor `user` on stdio and `host_admin` on HTTP, and `next: tell_user_to_run`. The mirror case: an MCP-only fix rendered for the CLI (a remote brain's fix on a thin client) keeps its `mcp` call as data, gets actor `user`, a `user_message` saying to call that tool over MCP, and `next: tell_user_to_run`; the human line reads `Fix: call over MCP with {…}`. ### Exclusive fixes and two-step plans `requires_exclusive: true` means the fix needs the brain's single-writer lock (`init --force --embedding-model`, `doctor --remediate`, `import`, `reindex-*`, `pglite-repair`, `migrate-embeddings`). Where gbrain can, it routes the work through the running `gbrain serve` that holds the lock and the fix just works. Otherwise the fix is a two-step plan: step one (actor `user`) stops the serve that owns the brain, and `then` carries the command to run once it has stopped. Run the steps in order and run `then.verify` at the end. ## Notices Notices are advice that rides a successful result: a degraded search, a truncated listing, a missing backup, a decision the user should make. ```ts interface RenderedNotice { code: string; // notice code kind: 'safety' | 'degraded' | 'coaching' | 'ask' | 'info'; why: string; fix?: RenderedAction; user_message?: string; decisions?: { id: string; question: string; options: { id: string; label: string; argv?: string[] }[]; default: string; default_reason: string }[]; contract_version: 1; } ``` **MCP success results.** `content[0]` is byte-identical to what it was before notices existed (bare arrays included). Each notice is one extra text block whose first line is the fixed prefix, then the fields that are set: ```text [gbrain notice kind=] why: fix: next: user_message: decision : (default:

# Connect GBrain to OpenClaw

> This page is the MCP-registration reference card. For the full brain install
> — CLI, engine, skills, dream cycle — follow
> [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md); the README covers the
> bootstrap and connect paths.

Connect with [Option 2](#option-2-openclaw-mcp-add) (stdio) when the brain runs on
the gateway's machine, or with
[OpenClaw's own MCP client](#remote-brain-openclaws-mcp-client-over-https) when it
runs elsewhere. Option 1's ClawHub bundle is not available yet.
A bot that several people DM connects over HTTP as well: see
[One bot for several people, in DMs](#one-bot-for-several-people-in-dms).

## Option 1: ClawHub bundle plugin (not available yet)

This project publishes no ClawHub package yet. The package named `gbrain` on
ClawHub is an unofficial upload of an old 0.10.1 build whose manifest has no
`id`, so `openclaw plugins install clawhub:gbrain` stops with
`plugin manifest requires id`. Don't install it; use Option 2.

GBrain ships [`openclaw.plugin.json`](../../openclaw.plugin.json) at the repo
root. Installing the bundle plugin registers the MCP server for you — the
manifest carries an `mcpServers.gbrain` entry that runs the bundled
`.agents/gbrain-launcher serve` (the same launcher the Codex and Claude Code
plugins use; it resolves your installed `gbrain` via `GBRAIN_BIN`, then
`~/.bun/bin/gbrain`, then `PATH`, so it works under launchd's bare PATH and
never needs a build step) plus the bundled skills — and declares the
`gbrain-context-engine` context engine. To route OpenClaw's context-engine slot
through gbrain, two steps, in this order:

1. Install and enable the plugin by its own id, `gbrain-context-engine`
   (the `id` in `openclaw.plugin.json`).
2. Set the slot to the engine id the plugin registers:

   ```
   plugins.slots.contextEngine = gbrain-context-engine
   ```

The current host requires the canonical plugin ID in the slot. The installed
plugin ID is unchanged and `gbrain-context` remains a registry alias for older
integrations, but it is not a slot alias on current hosts: migrate an old
`plugins.slots.contextEngine = gbrain-context` setting to
`gbrain-context-engine`. Setting the slot alone does not install/enable the
plugin. For a legacy host that cannot provide a per-session workspace, set
`plugins.entries.gbrain-context-engine.config.workspaceDir` to an absolute
workspace path; on multi-agent hosts prefer the host-supplied workspace. An
unbound or ambiguous workspace warns and reads no source rather than selecting
an arbitrary agent's memory.

The factory also accepts zero arguments from current hosts. Its `assemble`
keeps the current prompt separate from fenced stored transcript history; an
identical trailing legacy user message is already the current turn. The
admitted-turn acknowledgement is stateless and writes nothing. Reflex-only
pointer synthesis leaves returned messages unchanged; the turn acknowledgement
does not automatically capture conversation content (compaction has its own
explicit checkpoint path). Loading the plugin alone is not evidence of model
recall: verify saved-page retrieval after a restarted turn and source isolation
with the intended host. The loopback native test uses a deterministic provider,
so it does not certify paid-model recall or provenance.

## Option 2: `openclaw mcp add`

OpenClaw keeps MCP servers under `mcp.servers` in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`
(`openclaw config schema` shows the key path). Register gbrain with the CLI,
then run `gbrain setup openclaw` so a new session knows to use it:

```bash
openclaw mcp add gbrain --command "$(command -v gbrain)" --arg serve --arg --surface --arg starter --arg --advertise --arg verbs --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME
gbrain setup openclaw
```

The second line is not optional. Without it the tools are registered but
nothing tells the agent to use them, and a new session answers from OpenClaw's
own memory and chat history instead (in the [install eval](https://github.com/garrytan/harness-evals/blob/master/docs/benchmarks/2026-11-17-gbrain-install/results/README.md),
11 of the 30 OpenClaw runs without gbrain's install block missed this way).
See [Brain-first instructions](#brain-first-instructions).

Use an absolute `--command` path: the launchd-started gateway's `PATH` does
not include `~/.bun/bin`, so a bare `gbrain` fails to spawn. `--env` is
optional: a PGLite brain needs no `DATABASE_URL`
(`--env DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...` for Postgres), and `GBRAIN_HOME` only
matters when the brain home isn't `~/.gbrain`. `--surface starter --advertise verbs`
lists the seven-verb memory protocol ([MEMORY_VERBS v1](../protocol/MEMORY_VERBS_v1.md))
plus `request_tools`, which reaches every other tool; drop the
`--advertise verbs` values to list the starter set (`full` for the whole catalog) (check
`openclaw mcp add --help` for your version's `--arg` spelling).

Leave `GBRAIN_SOURCE` unset in the MCP env unless you deliberately want
single-source retrieval: a pin scopes every tool (search, `get_brain_identity`
counts, …) to that one source, and nothing warns on reads.

## Remote brain: OpenClaw's MCP client over HTTPS

When the brain runs on another machine, OpenClaw connects to its MCP endpoint
itself, over streamable HTTP with OAuth. That grant is scoped and revocable on
the brain host, while the stdio route above gives the gateway full local
database access.

```bash
openclaw gateway stop
openclaw mcp add gbrain --url https://<brain-host>/mcp --transport streamable-http --auth oauth
openclaw mcp login gbrain
openclaw mcp doctor gbrain --probe
openclaw gateway start
```

`mcp add`, `login` and `doctor --probe` refuse while the local gateway runs, so
stop it first and start it again after. `openclaw mcp login` runs the browser sign-in (on a headless host it prints a
`--code` command to finish with). OpenClaw registers its client through dynamic
client registration, so the brain owner turns that on and approves the consent
([native OAuth path](../guides/hosted-harness-access.md#native-oauth-path),
[self-service registration](ADMIN.md#self-service-dynamic-registration)). Until
the login succeeds, OpenClaw leaves the server out of agent turns. Publish the
endpoint with `gbrain mcp expose` ([remote MCP](../guides/remote-mcp.md)).

### Or: a thin client's stdio bridge

When OpenClaw should keep a stdio entry, install gbrain on the OpenClaw
machine as a thin client of the brain host and register its `gbrain serve`,
which relays every call to the host with that client's grant (it opens no
local database). On the brain host, `gbrain agent register` with
`--harness openclaw` prints these lines with your client filled in; run them
on the OpenClaw machine:

```bash
gbrain init --mcp-only --issuer-url https://<brain-host> --mcp-url https://<brain-host>/mcp \
  --oauth-client-id <client_id> --oauth-client-secret <client_secret>
openclaw mcp add gbrain --command "$(command -v gbrain)" --arg serve --arg --surface --arg starter --arg --advertise --arg verbs
```

If gbrain's bundle plugin is installed there, it already registers gbrain:
run only the `init` line. To keep this client apart from another gbrain on
that machine, put `GBRAIN_HOME=<dir>` before the `init` line and add
`--env GBRAIN_HOME=<dir>` to the `mcp add` line. What the bridge relays and
how it reports failures: [stdio bridge](../architecture/thin-client.md#stdio-bridge).

## One bot for several people, in DMs

When one OpenClaw bot answers several people, each in their own DM, each DM can
read only the pages that person may read. The bot speaks to the brain as a
[shared agent](../tutorials/company-brain.md#two-scoping-models-pick-the-one-that-matches-your-shape):
every call carries an `X-Gbrain-On-Behalf-Of` header naming the person, and the
brain answers with that person's view, within the bot's own source grant. On
OpenClaw a small plugin sets the header from the DM's sender through the
[requester-scoped MCP connection resolver](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure)
(`api.registerMcpServerConnectionResolver`). OpenClaw supplies the sender, not
the model, and the header rides on the transport; an audience put in tool
arguments is refused (`on_behalf_of_in_arguments`).

**Say to your agent:** *"Set up my OpenClaw bot so each DM reads only what that
person may read"*, then *"Show what alice-example's DMs can read"* (it runs
`gbrain access check --token *** --as alice-example` on the brain host).

**DMs only.** The resolver learns who sent the turn (`requesterSenderId`, with
`messageChannel` and `agentAccountId`), not whether the turn came from a group
or who else is in it. On a group turn the sender's view would be shown to the
whole group. Use this recipe only on a gateway where every conversation has one
person in it: set [`groupPolicy: "disabled"`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/groups)
on each channel and turn `dm.groupEnabled` off on Discord and Slack. Group
audiences are tracked in #8534.

### Before you share a personal brain through the bot

Each DM reads as one member, so anything that relaxes privacy for a single
member relaxes it for every person the bot serves:

- **No private-pages grant on the bot.** Never give its token
  `--private-pages granted-sources`. With it, every mapped person reads every
  `visibility: private` page in the bot's sources, which on a personal brain are
  your own private pages.
- **No private-facts grant on the bot.** Leave its token at
  `--private-facts none`. A DM call that names a person never uses that grant
  (an asserted audience reads world-only facts), so it adds nothing for the
  people the bot serves, and any call that reaches the brain without the header
  would read every fact saved private in the bot's sources.
- **Host hatches off.** `GBRAIN_REMOTE_PRIVATE_PAGES` and
  `search.remote_private_pages` apply to every remote caller on the host, this
  bot included. Leave both unset while the bot runs.
- **A dedicated token bound to no member.** Make a new token for the bot. Don't
  reuse your own agent's token or bind the bot's token to your member: your DMs
  through the bot then read like anyone else's, and your own agent keeps your
  full view.
- **Pages only you should read name you as their reader.** Today `access:
  private` and `visibility: private` hide a page from this bot. Clearing those
  labels, by hand or in bulk with `gbrain repair private-labels`, makes the
  pages readable in every DM and by `guest`. Before you clear them, give the
  pages you want to keep to yourself `readable_by: [<your member>]` or a folder
  rule (`gbrain access rule add --prefix <folder>/ --readers <your member>`).

`gbrain access check --token *** --as <member>` must show
`Private pages: none` for the bot.

### Keep the gateway's people apart too

The header separates the brain's answers. The rest of the gateway has to keep
people apart as well
([OpenClaw's trust model](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security/trust-model)
treats one gateway as one trust boundary, so people who must not trust each
other need separate gateways):

- [`session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/session)
  (`per-account-channel-peer` with several accounts on one channel). The default,
  `main`, puts every DM in one session, so one person's brain results land in
  the next person's context.
- `tools.sessions.visibility: "self"`, so session tools can't read another
  person's DM transcript.
- No shell or file tools for this agent on the gateway host: commands there
  inherit the gateway's environment, which holds the bot's token, and a local
  `gbrain` or database URL reads every page.
- Leave the `gbrain-context-engine` slot unset for this bot. It reads through
  the host's own brain connection, not the bot's token.

### On the brain host

Run `gbrain serve --http` ([deploy guide](DEPLOY.md)). Add each person as a
member, make a read-only token for the bot, and list whom it may act for: each
person's member id, plus `guest` for senders who have none. Never `*`.

```bash
gbrain access member add alice-example
gbrain access member add bob-example
gbrain auth create openclaw-dm-bot --scopes read     # prints the token once
gbrain auth rescope --token *** --sources <source-id> --may-act-for alice-example,bob-example,guest
gbrain access check --token *** --as alice-example
```

**Keep the token read-only.** An audience limits which existing pages a write
can reach, not where a new page lands. A write-capable token keeps its own
write grant whatever the header says, so a page made in one DM outside a ruled
folder (a new top-level page, a `capture` into `inbox/`) is read by everyone
the source admits, `guest` included, unless the write names `readable_by`,
which is the model's choice and not a fence. If the bot has to write for people
who must not affect each other's data, register one client per person with
`--bound-slug-prefixes <their folder>/`
([Model B](../tutorials/company-brain.md#two-scoping-models-pick-the-one-that-matches-your-shape));
the resolver can return each sender's own credential.

content.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

platform=$(uname -ms)

if [[ ${OS:-} = Windows_NT ]]; then
  if [[ $platform != MINGW64* ]]; then
    powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1|iex"
    exit $?
  fi
fi

# Reset
Color_Off=''

# Regular Colors
Red=''
Green=''
Dim='' # White

# Bold
Bold_White=''
Bold_Green=''

if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    # Reset
    Color_Off='\033[0m' # Text Reset

    # Regular Colors
    Red='\033[0;31m'   # Red
    Green='\033[0;32m' # Green
    Dim='\033[0;2m'    # White

    # Bold
    Bold_Green='\033[1;32m' # Bold Green
    Bold_White='\033[1m'    # Bold White
fi

error() {
    echo -e "${Red}error${Color_Off}:" "$@" >&2
    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${Dim}$@ ${Color_Off}"
}

info_bold() {
    echo -e "${Bold_White}$@ ${Color_Off}"
}

success() {
    echo -e "${Green}$@ ${Color_Off}"
}

command -v unzip >/dev/null ||
    error 'unzip is required to install bun'

if [[ $# -gt 2 ]]; then
    error 'Too many arguments, only 2 are allowed. The first can be a specific tag of bun to install. (e.g. "bun-v0.1.4") The second can be a build variant of bun to install. (e.g. "debug-info")'
fi

case $platform in
'Darwin x86_64')
    target=darwin-x64
    ;;
'Darwin arm64')
    target=darwin-aarch64
    ;;
'Linux aarch64' | 'Linux arm64')
    target=linux-aarch64
    ;;
'MINGW64'*'ARM64'* | 'MINGW64'*'aarch64'*)
    target=windows-aarch64
    ;;
'MINGW64'*)
    target=windows-x64
    ;;
'Linux riscv64')
    error 'Not supported on riscv64'
    ;;
'Linux x86_64' | *)
    target=linux-x64
    ;;
esac

case "$target" in
'linux'*)
    if [ -f /etc/alpine-release ]; then
        target="$target-musl"
    fi
    ;;
esac

if [[ $target = darwin-x64 ]]; then
    # Is this process running in Rosetta?
    # redirect stderr to devnull to avoid error message when not running in Rosetta
    if [[ $(sysctl -n sysctl.proc_translated 2>/dev/null) = 1 ]]; then
        target=darwin-aarch64
        info "Your shell is running in Rosetta 2. Downloading bun for $target instead"
    fi
fi

GITHUB=${GITHUB-"https://github.com"}

github_repo="$GITHUB/oven-sh/bun"

# A pinned older version ($1) may still split haswell/nehalem; probe AVX2 and
# request `-baseline` on miss. Current releases alias that name.
case "$target" in
'darwin-x64'*)
    if [[ $(sysctl -a | grep machdep.cpu | grep AVX2) == '' ]]; then
        target="$target-baseline"
    fi
    ;;
'linux-x64'*)
    if [[ $(cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep avx2) = '' ]]; then
        target="$target-baseline"
    fi
    ;;
esac

exe_name=bun

if [[ $# = 2 && $2 = debug-info ]]; then
    target=$target-profile
    exe_name=bun-profile
    info "You requested a debug build of bun. More information will be shown if a crash occurs."
fi

if [[ $# = 0 ]]; then
    bun_uri=$github_repo/releases/latest/download/bun-$target.zip
else
    bun_uri=$github_repo/releases/download/$1/bun-$target.zip
fi

install_env=BUN_INSTALL
bin_env=\$$install_env/bin

install_dir=${!install_env:-$HOME/.bun}
bin_dir=$install_dir/bin
exe=$bin_dir/bun

if [[ ! -d $bin_dir ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$bin_dir" ||
        error "Failed to create install directory \"$bin_dir\""
fi

curl --fail --location --progress-bar --output "$exe.zip" "$bun_uri" ||
    error "Failed to download bun from \"$bun_uri\""

unzip -oqd "$bin_dir" "$exe.zip" ||
    error 'Failed to extract bun'

mv "$bin_dir/bun-$target/$exe_name" "$exe" ||
    error 'Failed to move extracted bun to destination'

chmod +x "$exe" ||
    error 'Failed to set permissions on bun executable'

rm -r "$bin_dir/bun-$target" "$exe.zip"

tildify() {
    if [[ $1 = $HOME/* ]]; then
        local replacement=\~/

        echo "${1/$HOME\//$replacement}"
    else
        echo "$1"
    fi
}

success "bun was installed successfully to $Bold_Green$(tildify "$exe")"

if command -v bun >/dev/null; then
    # Install completions, but we don't care if it fails
    IS_BUN_AUTO_UPDATE=true $exe completions &>/dev/null || :

    echo "Run 'bun --help' to get started"
    exit
fi

refresh_command=''

tilde_bin_dir=$(tildify "$bin_dir")
quoted_install_dir=\"${install_dir//\"/\\\"}\"

if [[ $quoted_install_dir = \"$HOME/* ]]; then
    quoted_install_dir=${quoted_install_dir/$HOME\//\$HOME/}
fi

echo

case $(basename "$SHELL") in
fish)
    # Install completions, but we don't care if it fails
    IS_BUN_AUTO_UPDATE=true SHELL=fish $exe completions &>/dev/null || :

    commands=(
        "set --export $install_env $quoted_install_dir"
        "set --export PATH $bin_env \$PATH"
    )

    fish_config=$HOME/.config/fish/config.fish
    tilde_fish_config=$(tildify "$fish_config")

    if [[ -w $fish_config ]]; then
        {
            echo -e '\n# bun'

            for command in "${commands[@]}"; do
                echo "$command"
            done
        } >>"$fish_config"

        info "Added \"$tilde_bin_dir\" to \$PATH in \"$tilde_fish_config\""

        refresh_command="source $tilde_fish_config"
    else
        echo "Manually add the directory to $tilde_fish_config (or similar):"

        for command in "${commands[@]}"; do
            info_bold "  $command"
        done
    fi
    ;;
zsh)
    # Install completions, but we don't care if it fails
    IS_BUN_AUTO_UPDATE=true SHELL=zsh $exe completions &>/dev/null || :

    commands=(
        "export $install_env=$quoted_install_dir"
        "export PATH=\"$bin_env:\$PATH\""
    )

    zsh_config=$HOME/.zshrc
    tilde_zsh_config=$(tildify "$zsh_config")

    if [[ -w $zsh_config ]]; then
        {
            echo -e '\n# bun'

            for command in "${commands[@]}"; do
                echo "$command"
            done
        } >>"$zsh_config"

        info "Added \"$tilde_bin_dir\" to \$PATH in \"$tilde_zsh_config\""

        refresh_command="exec $SHELL"
    else
        echo "Manually add the directory to $tilde_zsh_config (or similar):"

        for command in "${commands[@]}"; do
            info_bold "  $command"
        done
    fi
    ;;
bash)
    # Install completions, but we don't care if it fails
    IS_BUN_AUTO_UPDATE=true SHELL=bash $exe completions &>/dev/null || :

    commands=(
        "export $install_env=$quoted_install_dir"
        "export PATH=\"$bin_env:\$PATH\""
    )

    bash_configs=(
        "$HOME/.bash_profile"
        "$HOME/.bashrc"
    )

    if [[ ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-} ]]; then
        bash_configs+=(
            "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bash_profile"
            "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bashrc"
            "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bash_profile"
            "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bashrc"
        )
    fi

    set_manually=true
    for bash_config in "${bash_configs[@]}"; do
        tilde_bash_config=$(tildify "$bash_config")

        if [[ -w $bash_config ]]; then
            {
                echo -e '\n# bun'

                for command in "${commands[@]}"; do
                    echo "$command"
                done
            } >>"$bash_config"

            info "Added \"$tilde_bin_dir\" to \$PATH in \"$tilde_bash_config\""

            refresh_command="source $bash_config"
            set_manually=false
            break
        fi
    done

    if [[ $set_manually = true ]]; then
        echo "Manually add the directory to $tilde_bash_config (or similar):"

        for command in "${commands[@]}"; do
            info_bold "  $command"
        done
    fi
    ;;
*)
    echo 'Manually add the directory to ~/.bashrc (or similar):'
    info_bold "  export $install_env=$quoted_install_dir"
    info_bold "  export PATH=\"$bin_env:\$PATH\""
    ;;
esac

echo
info "To get started, run:"
echo

if [[ $refresh_command ]]; then
    info_bold "  $refresh_command"
fi

info_bold "  bun --help"

arguments.command:
for f in "$HOME/.bash_profile" "$HOME/.bashrc" "$HOME/.profile"; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then printf '
--- %s ---
' "$f"; cat "$f"; fi; done; printf '
--- PATH ---
%s
' "$PATH"; bash /tmp/gbrain-bun-install.sh; export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"; bun --version; GBRAIN_NO_AUTOPILOT_INSTALL=1 GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1 bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.760.0

arguments.title: Read brain-first setup behavior and skill routing

content.text:
### What each DM gets

- A mapped sender reads as their member: the pages every member may read, plus
  pages whose `readable_by` or folder rule lists them, within the bot's sources.
- An unmapped sender reads as `guest`: no restricted page and no private page.
  To give unmapped senders no brain at all, return `null` from `resolve` when
  `members` has no entry for the sender.
- A mapped member outside `--may-act-for` is refused
  (`on_behalf_of_not_permitted`), and one that names no enabled member is refused
  (`on_behalf_of_unknown_member`); nothing is read either way
  ([shared-agent refusals](../guides/write-refusals.md#shared-agent-refusals)).
- Runs without a trusted sender (cron, heartbeat, subagents) get no gbrain
  server from the resolver. Scheduled jobs that use the
  [wrapper below](#scheduled-jobs-and-workspace-scripts) read as the brain
  owner, so never send their output to someone's DM.

To stop the bot reading for someone, take them out of `--may-act-for`. gbrain
reads that list on every call; OpenClaw may keep a resolved connection for a
few minutes. To check from a DM, ask the bot to call `whoami`: its
`access.applied` names the audience the call read as, and `relaxation` must
read `none`.

## Brain-first instructions

Registering the server only makes the tools available. Agents seldom call a
brain nobody told them about, so finish either option with the primary route,
the per-turn rule:

```bash
gbrain setup openclaw   # --dry-run previews; --workspace <dir> picks the agent
```

It writes one short marked block into the workspace `AGENTS.md` (from
`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` or `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`: a sole agent's
workspace, else `agents.defaults.workspace`, else `~/.openclaw/workspace`; with
several agents, pass `--workspace`). Text outside the markers is never touched,
a re-run upgrades the block in place, `--no-instructions` opts out and is
remembered, and `--remove` takes it out. A thin-client install puts the same
block at the top of `GBRAIN-INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

A rule in `AGENTS.md` reaches the system prompt only, so setup also puts it next
to every user turn with a hook-only OpenClaw plugin, `gbrain-turn-rule`: its
`before_prompt_build` handler returns the rule as `prependContext` (without its
closing "answer" sentence on heartbeat, cron and exec-completion turns). The plugin is
self-contained (the rule text is in its code; it reads and calls nothing) and
lives in `<OpenClaw state dir>/gbrain/gbrain-turn-rule`. Setup installs it with
OpenClaw's own CLI:

```bash
openclaw plugins install --link <state dir>/gbrain/gbrain-turn-rule --force --accept-capabilities
openclaw plugins enable gbrain-turn-rule
openclaw config set plugins.entries.gbrain-turn-rule.hooks.allowConversationAccess true
```

OpenClaw requires `allowConversationAccess` before a non-bundled plugin's
`before_prompt_build` runs. With no `openclaw` on PATH, setup writes the plugin
and prints those commands to run on the OpenClaw host; restart a running gateway
afterwards. `--no-instructions` and `--remove` uninstall the plugin and delete
its directory. A re-run after an upgrade rewrites the plugin with the new text.
Every agent on the gateway gets the plugin's rule, so a `--workspace` run leaves
it when it would name another server and `--no-instructions` there keeps it.

OpenClaw lists no gbrain tool after `openclaw mcp set`: the model reaches them
only through `tool_search`, whose results it frames as external data. With an
MCP connection the rule therefore names the tools (`recall`, `entity`, `search`,
`query`) and says to find them with `tool_search` and run them with `tool_call`.
With `openclaw` on PATH, setup runs
`openclaw plugins inspect gbrain-turn-rule --runtime --json` and exits non-zero
with `turn_hook_not_loaded` unless the plugin shows as loaded with
`before_prompt_build` ([repair](../guides/repair.md#turn-hook-not-loaded)).

## Skills (fallback)

`gbrain skillpack scaffold --harness openclaw` adds gbrain's skills to the
workspace. OpenClaw lists them in its prompt, but in harness-evals a listed
skill was followed on 1-3% of turns against 97-100% for the per-turn rule, so
install skills beside the rule, never instead of it. OpenClaw serves a skill
only whole: a SKILL.md larger than one read (64,000 characters on a model with
200k+ context, 32,000 at 100k-200k, 16,000 below, a 32,768-byte page when the
context window is unknown) gets "cannot be partially served" and nothing else.
Every SKILL.md gbrain installs for OpenClaw is at most 32,000 bytes
(`test/openclaw-route.test.ts`), so it loads on any model with 100k+ context
and when the window is unknown; on smaller models the 16,000-character cap
applies and the larger skills do not load.

## Scheduled jobs and workspace scripts

OpenClaw cron jobs, workspace scripts and hooks run with another `HOME` and
environment than the gateway's MCP server. Route every one of them through a
single wrapper that sets `GBRAIN_HOME`, loads the brain's env file and runs the
installed `gbrain` by absolute path; log its stderr and check its exit code
([the wrapper and its rules](../guides/cron-schedule.md#calling-gbrain-unattended)).
On a managed brain, scripts commit the files they write with
`gbrain git commit-push -- <paths>` (never plain `git commit`); a scheduled
`gbrain sources refresh <id>`
keeps it current
([scripts and the managed checkout](../guides/shared-checkout-git.md#scripts-and-the-managed-checkout)).

## Have gbrain report back to this chat

When the brain owner has turned on [reporting back](../guides/wakeshift.md)
(`gbrain wakeshift enable` on the brain host), gbrain can wake an OpenClaw
session when a job, a pending write or a cron run it watches finishes. OpenClaw
needs Wakeshift's own plugin for that. Where the gateway runs (in its container,
if it's in one):

```bash
gbrain setup openclaw --wakeshift
```

It asks for consent, then runs OpenClaw's installer for the pinned
`@wakeshift/openclaw@1.4.31` (`openclaw plugins install npm:@wakeshift/openclaw@1.4.31 --force --accept-capabilities`,
then `openclaw plugins enable wakeshift --accept-capabilities`) and checks that
the plugin loads. The plugin turns on OpenClaw's hooks endpoint with its own
token. On a gateway that listens beyond this computer, setup prints
Wakeshift's question about that endpoint; agreeing is yours to do
(`openclaw config set plugins.entries.wakeshift.config.allowNetworkHooks true --strict-json`),
and gbrain never sets it. The session shows a note starting `Wakeshift: connected`
after its first watch. `gbrain doctor` warns when the installed plugin is not
the pinned version. Remove it with
`openclaw wakeshift reset && openclaw plugins uninstall wakeshift --force`.

## Verify

`openclaw mcp list` should show `gbrain`. Then start an agent turn and ask it
to use the brain:

```
Call get_brain_identity, then search my brain for [topic].
```

If the tools respond, the wiring works. `list_skills` shows everything the
brain can do (gated by `mcp.publish_skills` on the host).

## Remove

Delete `mcp.servers.gbrain` from `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (or run
`openclaw mcp remove gbrain` if your version has it), or uninstall the bundle
plugin.
# GBrain Skill Resolver

This is the dispatcher. Skills are the implementation. **Read the skill file before acting.** If two skills could match, read both. They are designed to chain (e.g., ingest then enrich for each entity).

**Routing contract:** each skill's frontmatter `triggers:` array is the
authoritative routing signal — harnesses match inbound messages against it
(see `skills/_AGENT_README.md`). This file is the human-readable dispatch
map of the same routing: one place to scan every skill and its trigger
phrases. If a row here and a skill's frontmatter disagree, the frontmatter
wins; fix the row.

**A gbrain call failed or printed `[AGENT]` or a notice block:** follow the
[agent operator protocol](./conventions/agent-operator-protocol.md). Read the
error's `code` (fall back to `error`), follow `fix.next`, then run `fix.verify`.

## Which gbrain call for which lookup

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED lookup-table (copied from skills/conventions/brain-first.md by bun run regen:all) -->
Ask gbrain before you `grep`, `cat`, `ls` or run SQL on the brain checkout: it
reads the index across every source, ranks, filters and names the slug to read
next. With the gbrain MCP server connected, call the tool of the same name
instead of the CLI (one connection, no per-call startup).

| Lookup | CLI | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| Find a page by name or path | `gbrain find <name\|prefix\|glob> [--type T] [--source S]` | `find_pages` |
| Count pages by kind or source | `gbrain stats --by source,type [--since 30d] [--collapse-aliases]` | `get_stats` (needs an admin-scope token) |
| Answer a question, search a topic | `gbrain query "<question>" [--types '["meeting"]'] [--since 30d]` | `query` |
| Pages with these words | `gbrain search "<words>" [--match keyword] [--source S]` | `search` |
| Read a known page | `gbrain get <slug>` | `get_page` |
| Read only the part a search hit points at | `gbrain get <slug> --around-chunk-id <chunk_id>` or `--lines '{"from":1,"count":200}'` | `get_page` |
| What the brain knows about a person or company | `gbrain entity <slug>`, then `gbrain recall "<topic>" --json` | `entity`, `recall` |
| Links, dated events, every page of a type | `gbrain backlinks <slug>`, `gbrain timeline <slug>`, `gbrain list --type T` | `get_backlinks`, `get_timeline`, `list_pages` |
| Save a fact the user stated | `gbrain remember "<fact>" --entity <slug> --content-origin user_said --provenance "<where>"` | `remember` |
| Why a page didn't rank | `gbrain query "<q>" --explain-target <slug>` | `query` |
| Which installed skill fits a request | `gbrain skills resolve --text "<request>" --json` (after `gbrain skills index build`) | none (CLI only) |
| Find something archived to B2, Supabase or S3 | `gbrain storage-find "<phrase>"` | `storage_find` |

Parse `--json` output instead of matching the text; notices go to stderr. Never
send stderr to `/dev/null`: a refusal there (`no_brain`, `GBRAIN_DB_ACCESS`)
then reads as "no results"; check the exit code too. Take
`chunk_id` from a fresh `search --json` hit (an old one fails `revision_changed`),
and read a degraded notice before concluding the brain has nothing.
<!-- END GENERATED lookup-table -->

## Memory defaults

Preserve the existing agent's identity and instructions. Ordinary setup adds
keyless memory; personal-agent bootstrap requires an explicit request. Recall
and explicit remembering do not require automatic capture. Ambient capture is
off until the user opts in, and paid enrichment is a separate choice.

## Always-on recall and opt-in capture

| Trigger | Skill |
|---------|-------|
| Every substantive inbound message, only after automatic-capture opt-in | `skills/signal-detector/SKILL.md` (delegation additionally requires authorization) |
| Any brain read/write/lookup/citation | `skills/brain-ops/SKILL.md` |

## Brain operations

| Trigger | Skill |
|---------|-------|
| "What do we know about", "tell me about", "search for", "who is", "background on", "notes on" | `skills/query/SKILL.md` |
| "Who knows who", "relationship between", "connections", "graph query" | `skills/query/SKILL.md` (use graph-query) |
| Creating/enriching a person or company page | `skills/enrich/SKILL.md` |

content.text:
/** How the agent reaches the brain, which decides the tool names the block uses. */
export type BrainFirstAccess = { kind: 'mcp'; server: string; surface?: McpSurface; serves?: 'several' } | { kind: 'cli'; launcher: string };

/** GST-363: on a brain that serves several people the connection is bound to the person asking, so the agent does no scoping of its own. */
export const SERVES_SEVERAL_LINE = 'This connection reads only what the person asking may read.';

/** The block interior (without markers). */
export function renderBrainFirstBlock(harness: string, access: BrainFirstAccess, optOut = `gbrain setup ${harness} --instructions-only --no-instructions`): string {
  const tool = (mcp: string, cli: string) => (access.kind === 'mcp' ? `\`${mcp}\`` : `\`${access.launcher} ${cli}\``);
  const where = access.kind === 'mcp' ? `the \`${access.server}\` MCP server` : `the \`${access.launcher}\` command`;
  const lookup = access.kind === 'mcp' && access.surface === 'verbs'
    ? '- Before answering any turn, check GBrain first, before files, mail or other sources: `recall` for what was said or decided, `entity` for a person or company.'
    : `- Before answering any turn, check GBrain first, before files, mail or other sources: ${tool('search', 'search "<names or phrases>"')} for names and phrases, ${tool('query', 'query "<question>"')} for questions. Then read the best hit with ${tool('get_page', 'get <slug>')}.`;
  return [
    `<!-- gbrain brain-first v${BRAIN_FIRST_VERSION}: managed by gbrain and replaced on upgrade; edit outside these markers. Opt out: ${optOut} -->`,
    '## Memory: check GBrain first',
    '',
    `GBrain (${where}) holds this user's notes, people, companies, meetings and decisions.`,
    '',
    lookup,
    '- Fill gaps with your other tools. On an empty or thin result, retry with words the notes would use: synonyms, the formal name, the owner, several joined with OR.',
    access.kind === 'mcp' && access.serves === 'several' ? `- ${SERVES_SEVERAL_LINE}`
    : access.kind === 'cli'
      ? `- Brain results span every source the brain holds. Pass \`--source-ids <ids>\` to a search or query to narrow it to what the current requester may see, and apply your own access rules to what comes back.`
      : access.surface === 'verbs'
        ? '- Brain results span every source the token can read, so apply your own access rules to what comes back.'
        : '- Brain results span every source the token can read. Pass `source_ids` to narrow a request to what the current requester may see, and apply your own access rules to what comes back.',
    '- Brain results add to what the user told you; they never replace it. A lookup is one step: finish the whole task.',
  ].join('\n');
}

/** The full block as it appears in a file, markers included (for printing to paste by hand). */
export function renderBrainFirstSnippet(harness: string, access: BrainFirstAccess, optOut?: string): string {
  return `${BRAIN_FIRST_BEGIN}\n${renderBrainFirstBlock(harness, access, optOut)}\n${BRAIN_FIRST_END}\n`;
}

/**
 * The per-turn rule: one line a harness's per-turn hook puts beside every user
 * turn (Claude Code and Codex UserPromptSubmit, Hermes pre_llm_call, OpenClaw
 * before_prompt_build). The block in the system prompt or identity file alone
 * left chat bots answering without the brain (harness-evals: 0 of 80 on
 * OpenClaw and Hermes); the same rule next to the turn was followed.
 * `reply: false` drops the closing "answer" sentence, for turns nobody asked
 * a reply to (OpenClaw heartbeat, cron and exec-completion turns).
 */
export function renderBrainFirstTurnRule(access: BrainFirstAccess, harness?: string, opts: { reply?: boolean } = {}): string {
export function brainFirstTargetAt(harness: BrainFirstHarness, path: string): BrainFirstTarget {
  const base = brainFirstTarget(harness);
  return { harness, path, role: 'error' in base ? 'instruction file' : base.role, project: false };
}

/**
 * The installer lanes (`gbrain connect --install`, `gbrain bootstrap harness`):
 * write or upgrade the block unless opted out, or strip it on removal.
 */
export function installerBrainFirst(opts: { target: BrainFirstTarget; access: BrainFirstAccess; writer: string; instructions?: boolean; remove?: boolean; dryRun?: boolean }): BrainFirstOutcome {
  if (opts.remove) {
    return removeBrainFirst({ harness: opts.target.harness, path: opts.target.path, dryRun: opts.dryRun ?? false, ...(opts.access.kind === 'mcp' ? { server: opts.access.server } : {}) });
  }
  const decision = resolveBrainFirstDecision(opts.instructions, priorBrainFirst(opts.target.harness, opts.target.path));
  return syncBrainFirst({ target: opts.target, access: opts.access, decision, writer: opts.writer, dryRun: opts.dryRun ?? false });
}

/** One human line per outcome, matching setup's step lines. */
export function describeBrainFirstOutcome(o: BrainFirstOutcome, dryRun: boolean): string {
  return `  ${(dryRun && o.action !== 'keep' && o.action !== 'skip' ? `would ${o.action}` : o.action).padEnd(8)} ${'instructions'.padEnd(7)} ${o.detail}`;
